solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Be thankful for increase in value

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to value or be grateful for something
second meaning: to rise in worth, as property or shares do

explanation.surface: Someone grateful that an investment has gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both gratitude for a kindness and an asset gaining in price over time.

clue.text: Warning light in Wokingham, Berks

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the place names that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the town and the start of the county

explanation.surface: A traffic light seen in a Berkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Wokingham is a town in Berkshire, often shortened to Berks.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle traffic light, between red and green, cautions drivers that a change is coming.

clue.text: Tenacity shown by salesman overturned separation

indicators.note: in a down entry, overturned means the word for the salesman is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
severance is a cutting off or parting

explanation.surface: A salesman showing determination after being knocked over and parted from something.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistence in carrying on despite difficulty is the synonym for tenacity.

clue.text: Vivacity of English knight touring US city

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so the first pair of letters wraps around the city

parts.note: the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An Englishman knighted, lively as he tours an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: English and knight together make EN, which goes around LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash and liveliness of style, a synonym for vivacity.

clue.text: Asian needing help turned up in lodging-place

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed inside the word for a lodging-place

parts.note: an inn offers rooms for travellers

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is read upwards, from its last letter back

explanation.surface: A traveller from Asia who arrives at a guest house needing assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from India is an Asian, a specific example standing for the general term.

clue.text: Underweight ruler's philosophy?

parts.note: a king is a ruler; the 's is read as 'is', joining the pieces

explanation.surface: Asks whether a thin monarch has a particular outlook on life.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: one's thinking can mean one's philosophy or line of reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's thinking is their set of views or reasoned outlook, which is what a philosophy is.

clue.text: A sight in bed, wearing glasses!

indicators.note: the sight is placed inside the word for a bed

parts.note: a spectacle is a striking sight

explanation.surface: Someone in bed with their glasses on cuts a comic figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reuses spectacles: the wordplay's sight is a spectacle, and the answer means having spectacles on.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespectacled is the adjective for a person who has glasses on their face.

clue.text: Stick around entrance to restaurant, but go without food

indicators.note: the word for stick goes around the selected letter

parts.note: a stave is a stout stick

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone loitering outside a restaurant yet not eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to suffer from lack of food, i.e. going hungry.

clue.text: Poet nursing curious aim to be pub employee

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the following letters are put into an odd order
to nurse is to hold close, so the poet holds the shuffled letters

explanation.surface: A poet with a strange ambition to work behind a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A barmaid is a woman who serves drinks in a pub, so she is one of its staff.

clue.text: Bungling players initially employed in popular film

indicators.note: employed in means put to use inside, so the letter goes within the film

parts.note: E.T., Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Clumsy actors given parts in a hit movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, so bungling is a synonym for clumsy, incompetent work.

clue.text: Grass certain ruminants brought back

indicators.note: brought back means turned round to read from its end to its start

parts.note: deer chew the cud, so they are ruminants

explanation.surface: Grazing animals being returned to their grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall water grass, a specific type of the general category.

clue.text: Birds sound contented mostly, finding flowering plant

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Birds making a happy noise in a garden among the blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden plant with spurred blue flowers, related to the delphinium.

clue.text: In part, merit reanimated African citizen

indicators.note: in part says the answer is only a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from after the first letter of merit to the middle of reanimated

explanation.surface: An African national's worth brought back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa, so one of its nationals is an African citizen.

clue.text: Direct animal on farm

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to guide or point the way
second meaning: a young castrated bull raised for beef

explanation.surface: An instruction to herd livestock on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for guiding and also a noun for a bullock reared for meat.

clue.text: Small gallery accommodating high-class sculpture

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so the gallery holds the next letter

parts.note: the Tate, London's famous art gallery
U means upper-class, the opposite of non-U

explanation.surface: A modest gallery making room for a smart piece of sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from a 1950s British distinction between U and non-U speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure, one kind of sculpture.

clue.text: Opening Henry found in Riviera resort

indicators.note: found in says one piece is located inside another

parts.note: Nice, the city on the French Riviera
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man named Henry finds an opportunity on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess or gap in a wall, and so an opening; also a suitable opening in a market.

clue.text: Seal, or young bird, do we hear?
Chap demanding a final song, perhaps

parts.note: an air is a tune, perhaps a song

explanation.surface: A man calling for one last number before the party ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Alastair is a man's name, and a chap is any man, so the general word stands for the specific one.

clue.text: Group of musicians prohibited on radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so this points to a word that sounds the same

explanation.surface: A pop group barred from the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is an ensemble of people playing instruments together.

clue.text: Out of fashion, being invited for a tryst

definitions.meaning: second meaning: taken out on a romantic outing

explanation.surface: Someone unfashionable being asked out on a romantic meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means behind the times, and is also the past participle of going out with someone romantically.

clue.text: Animal pen at end of lane? It's an eyesore!

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter

explanation.surface: A pigsty at the bottom of a lane spoils the view.
explanation.walkthrough: An eyesore is usually an ugly sight; here it is literally a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Mum or Dad's brother, a pawnbroker

definitions.meaning: second meaning: old slang for a pawnbroker

explanation.surface: A family member who runs a pawnshop.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle as slang for a pawnbroker is dated British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The relative is the familiar meaning; the pawnbroker sense is an old slang usage.

clue.text: Backing school, the French finally sent brief communication

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the school is read in reverse

parts.note: Eton, the famous English public school

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A school supporter writes a short message to the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for writing a short note, so a brief message.

clue.text: Girl was inclined to accept time alone

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the inclined word takes in the next letter

parts.note: tended means was inclined or disposed

explanation.surface: A girl who chose to take some time on her own.
explanation.definitionFit: Unattended means left without anyone watching or present, so on its own.
